architecture.mechanism: Centrifuge rotor failure arises from stress concentration and fatigue at structural discontinuities, which can be mitigated by optimizing rotor geometry and material distribution to reduce peak stress.
architecture.intervention: Redesign the benchtop centrifuge rotor and aerodynamic enclosure with filleted transitions, balanced mass distribution, and high-fatigue-strength alloy or composite, while integrating the imbalance sensor to detect residual asymmetry before it induces interlock or lid failure.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced peak stress and fatigue crack initiation, lower rotor imbalance, and fewer lid interlock failures under repeated high-speed operation with sealed micro-vials.
architecture.falsification_test: Run accelerated spin-cycle testing (e.g., 10,000 cycles at maximum rated speed) on optimized versus original rotor; measure vibration amplitude, inspect for cracks via dye penetrant, and record any lid interlock fault events; the optimized design must show statistically significant reduction in vibration and zero interlock failures.
